name: Orrath Baobab-Pomegranate Drift
description: A lightly carbonated blend of synth-baobab and pomegranate extract, brewed in small batches in the Tier 2 Midlake district. It sits somewhere between a juice and a soda — thicker than most, with a dusty-sweet finish.
flavor_profile: Earthy baobab base with jammy pomegranate, a faint chalky minerality, and a dry tartness on the back of the throat
cultural_context: Popular among Tier 2 workers who grew up with baobab-flavored anything and feel mid-tier fruit sodas have abandoned roots for novelty. Orrath has a loyal, quiet fanbase that doesn't post about it — they just buy it every week.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 corner store has been exclusively stocking Orrath for 30 years — the owner claims a handshake deal with the founder that no corponation has been able to break, despite attempts
A batch of Orrath from three months ago has been showing up at black-market stalls with an added unlisted ingredient — buyers report unusually vivid dreams
A food historian doing archival work claims Orrath's original recipe predates GLMZ's founding and was carried in by a refugee family — the current owners deny it, nervously
